history.dynasty: Gangas (9th c.); Cholas (11th c.); Hoysalas (13th c.); Vijayanagara; Wodeyars of Mysore; patronage by Tipu Sultan
history.period: 9th century CE onwards (over 1000 years); present grandeur from Chola-Hoysala-Vijayanagara-Wodeyar additions; nine-storey gopuram 1849
history.summary: CORRECTED CSV TOWN: this temple stands in Nanjangud (Nanjangudu) town on the right bank of the Kapila (Kabini) river, about 23-25 km south of Mysuru city - NOT in Mysore city as the CSV row reads. The Sri Nanjundeshwara (Srikanteshwara) Temple is the largest temple in Karnataka (approx. 50,000 sq ft, 160 x 385 ft) and is called 'Dakshina Kashi' (Varanasi of the South). Legend says Sage Gauthama/Parasurama installed a lingam here; the name Nanjundeshwara means 'the one who destroyed poison' (Nanju = poison), linked to Shiva consuming the Halahala poison and to a legend of Shiva destroying the venomous demon Kesian at the confluence of the Kapila, Koundini and Manikarnika rivers. The Gangas built the first small garbhagriha (9th c.); the Cholas built the inner sanctum (11th c.); the Hoysalas added the anterior mandapa and a dancing Ganapathi (13th c.); the Vijayanagara rulers added the Parvati and Narayana shrines and the brick-and-mortar shikhara; Dalavayi Vikramaraya built the Tulabhara mantapa and a stone Nandi in 1644; Krishnaraja Wodeyar III gifted two wooden chariots (1819) and, with his queen Devajammanni, funded the nine-storey 120-ft Dravidian gopuram (1849). Tipu Sultan, after his elephant's eye affliction was reportedly cured by the deity, gifted an emerald (maragatha) lingam and called the god 'Hakim Nanjunda'. The prakara holds some 122 deity images, 65-66 Shiva lingas of various sizes, and a sculpture of Krishnaraja Wodeyar III with his four wives. Devotees believe the deity cures diseases and washes away sins; Panchamirtha abhishekam, betel-leaf garlands and curd-rice nivedhana are characteristic offerings.

name: Nanjundeshwara Temple
town_description: Nanjangud (Nanjanagudu), a temple town in Mysuru district on the right bank of the Kapila (Kabini) river, about 23-25 km south of Mysuru city on the Mysuru-Ooty road. The town's name derives from the Nanjundeshwara Temple, Karnataka's largest temple; the Kapila river ghats beside the temple draw pilgrims for a purifying dip before darshan.

travel.airport: Mysuru Airport is the nearest airport (approx. 25-30 km); Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru is about 170 km away (verify distances).
travel.railway: Nanjangud Town railway station is about 25 km from Mysuru Junction (per Indian Railways data); regular trains connect Mysuru and Nanjangud.
travel.road: About 23-25 km south of Mysuru city on the Mysuru-Ooty road; frequent government buses, taxis and autos from Mysuru. The temple is on Rastrapathi Road in the town centre.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; weekdays between 6 AM and 1:30 PM and 4 PM to 9 PM. The Dodda Jatre (March-April) is the grandest spectacle but extremely crowded; Sundays, Mondays and full-moon days are also popular.
